1.word_for_word: षोडशे कालियस्योक्तो निग्रहो यमुना-ह्रदे । — In the sixteenth instance, the restraint of the Yamunā is mentioned by Kāliya.; तत्-पत्नीभिः स्तुतेनाथ कृष्णेनानुग्रहः कृतः ॥ — The wives of the king praised him, and Lord Kṛṣṇa showed him mercy.; हत्वा रासभ-दैतेयान् जग्ध्वा ताल-फलान्य् अलम् । — After killing the Rāsabha demons and eating the palm fruits, it is enough.; प्रीतोऽनृत्यत् फणा-रङ्गे कालियस्य कलानिधिः ॥ — The treasure of the arts of Kāliya danced in delight on the hooded stage.; उदवासयन् निःसारितवान् ॥१॥ — He drove them out and drove them out.
1.translation: In the sixteenth instance, the restraint of the Yamunā is mentioned by Kāliya. The wives of the king praised him, and Lord Kṛṣṇa showed him mercy. After killing the Rāsabha demons and eating the palm fruits, it is enough. The treasure of the arts of Kāliya danced in delight on the hooded stage. He drove them out and drove them out.

2.word_for_word: बहूनि युगान्य् आवसो यस्य तम् अहिम् । — The snake that has been inhabited for many ages.; स वै अहिर् अजल-चरोऽपि तस्मिन्न् अन्तर्-जले यथा येन प्रकारेण आसीत् । — That same snake, which moved in the water, was in that deep water in whatever way it was.; अथवा, बहूनि युगान्य् आवासो यथा भवति, तथा येन प्रकारेण स वै तत्रासीद् इति कथ्यताम् इति ॥२॥ — Or, tell me, as it is the dwelling place for many ages, and in what manner he was there.
2.translation: The snake that has been inhabited for many ages. That same snake, which moved in the water, was in that deep water in whatever way it was. Or, tell me, as it is the dwelling place for many ages, and in what manner he was there.

3.word_for_word: गोपालेन यद् उदारं चरितम् आचरितं, तद् एव्आमृतम् । — The generous character of the cowherd boy is the same as the nectar.; अतः कथ्यताम् इति ॥३॥ — Therefore, tell me.
3.translation: The generous character of the cowherd boy is the same as the nectar. Therefore, tell me.

4.word_for_word: श्रप्यमाणं पच्यमानं पयो यस्य सः । — The milk which is boiled and cooked.; अत उपरि गच्छन्तः खगा यस्मिन् पतन्ति ॥४॥ — Therefore the birds flying above it fall upon it.
4.translation: The milk which is boiled and cooked. Therefore the birds flying above it fall upon it.

5.word_for_word: किं च, विप्रुष्मता अम्बु-कण-युक्तेन विषोद-तरङ्ग-स्पर्शि-मारुतेन स्पृष्टा यस्य तीरगा म्रियन्ते, स ह्रद आसीद् इति ॥५॥ — What is more, it is said that the lake was a lake whose banks were touched by the wind, which was touched by the poisonous waves, which were full of particles of water, and whose banks were dying.
5.translation: What is more, it is said that the lake was a lake whose banks were touched by the wind, which was touched by the poisonous waves, which were full of particles of water, and whose banks were dying.

6.word_for_word: तं कालियम् । — That’s the black one.; चण्डो वेगो यस्य तद् विषम् एव वीर्यं यस्य तम् । — The one whose speed is fierce is the one whose semen is poisonous.; कदम्बम् इति । — Kadamba is the name.; भाविना श्री-कृष्ण-चरण-स्पर्श-भाग्येन स एकस् तत्-तीरे न शुष्कः इति ज्ञातव्यम् । — By the future fortune of touching the feet of Lord Kṛṣṇa, one should know that he alone is not dry on that shore.; अमृतम् आहरता गरुत्-मता क्रान्तत्वाद् इति च पुराणान्तरम् । — According to another Purāṇa, it is said that Garuḍa, who ate nectar, was confused.; आस्फोट्य बाहुं कर-तलेनाहत्य । — He exploded and hit his arm with the palm of his hand.; गाढा दृढं बद्धा रशना कटि-बन्धन-वस्त्रं येन सः ॥६॥ — He was tied tightly with a belt and a waistband.
6.translation: That’s the black one. The one whose speed is fierce is the one whose semen is poisonous. Kadamba is the name. By the future fortune of touching the feet of Lord Kṛṣṇa, one should know that he alone is not dry on that shore. According to another Purāṇa, it is said that Garuḍa, who ate nectar, was confused. He exploded and hit his arm with the palm of his hand. He was tied tightly with a belt and a waistband.

7.word_for_word: तदा सर्पस्य ह्रदः । — Then the snake’s lake.; पुरुष-श्रेष्ठस्य पतन-भारेण सङ्क्षोभितानाम् उरगाणां विषैर् उन्नतोऽम्बु-राशिर् यस्य सः । — The waters of the river are raised by the venom of snakes agitated by the weight of the fall of the best of men; विषेण कषायी-कृता भयं-करा ऊर्मयो यस्य सः । — The waves of which are frightening, made alkaline by poison.; पर्यक् परितो धावन् धनुः-शतं प्लुतः प्रसृतः । — Running around the park, he floated a hundred bows and spread out.; नैतच् चित्रम् इत्य् आह---अनन्त-बलस्येति ॥७॥ — This is not surprising, he argues, because of the infinite power.
7.translation: Then the snake’s lake. The waters of the river are raised by the venom of snakes agitated by the weight of the fall of the best of men The waves of which are frightening, made alkaline by poison. Running around the park, he floated a hundred bows and spread out. This is not surprising, he argues, because of the infinite power.

8.word_for_word: ह्रदे विहरतो भुज-दण्डाहतोदक-घोषं श्रुत्वा ततः स्व-सदनाभिभवं निरीक्ष्य तद् असहमानः सर्पः समसरत् समाजगाम ॥८॥ — While playing in the lake the serpent heard the sound of water being struck by the staff of his arms and then observing the attack on his house the serpent could not bear it and rushed towards the assembly
8.translation: While playing in the lake the serpent heard the sound of water being struck by the staff of his arms and then observing the attack on his house the serpent could not bear it and rushed towards the assembly

9.word_for_word: प्रेक्षणीयश् च सुकुमारश् च घन-वद् उज्ज्वलश् च तम् । — He was spectacular and delicate and bright like a cloud; श्रीवत्स-पीत-वसनं ह्रदे विहरतः श्रीवत्सेन संयुक्तम् उच्चलत् पीतं वस्त्रं यय तम् । — While he was playing in the lake, he was wearing a yellow robe called Śrīvatsa.; भुजया भोगेन चच्छाद अवेष्टयत् ॥९॥ — He covered her with his arm and wrapped her in pleasure.
9.translation: He was spectacular and delicate and bright like a cloud While he was playing in the lake, he was wearing a yellow robe called Śrīvatsa. He covered her with his arm and wrapped her in pleasure.

12.word_for_word: भुवि भू-कम्पादयः, दिवि उल्का-पातादयः, आत्मनि वाम-नेत्र-स्फुरणादयः । — Earthquakes on earth, meteor showers in the sky, and twinkling of the left eye in the self.; आसन्नं भयं शंसितुं शीलं येषां ते ॥१२॥ — Those whose character is to warn of the imminent fear.
12.translation: Earthquakes on earth, meteor showers in the sky, and twinkling of the left eye in the self. Those whose character is to warn of the imminent fear.

13-15.word_for_word: तान् आलक्ष्य गोकुलान् निर्जग्मुर् इति तृतीयेनान्वयः । — The third consequence is that they noticed them and went out to the cowsheds.; भयोद्विग्ना भय-हेतुभ्यो भीताः । — They are afraid of the causes of fear.; भयेन कम्पमाना इति वा ॥१३॥ — or trembling with fear.; न तं विदन्तीत्य् अतद्-विदः ॥१४॥ — They do not know Him, for they do not know Him.; पशु-वृत्तयो ऽतिवत्सलाः ॥१५॥ — They are very affectionate to animals.
13-15.translation: The third consequence is that they noticed them and went out to the cowsheds. They are afraid of the causes of fear. or trembling with fear. They do not know Him, for they do not know Him. They are very affectionate to animals.

16.word_for_word: कातरान् भीतान् ॥१६॥ — They were afraid and frightened.

17.word_for_word: भगवन्तं लक्षयन्ति यानि पदानि, तैः पदैः सूचितया पदव्य-मार्गेण ॥१७॥ — The steps which perceive the Lord, by the path of the path indicated by those steps.
17.translation: The steps which perceive the Lord, by the path of the path indicated by those steps.

18.word_for_word: पदैर् मार्ग-ज्ञान-प्रकारम् आह---त इति । — He argues the type of path-knowledge in terms: ta.; विश्पतेः श्री-कृष्णस्य अन्येषां पदानाम् अन्तरान्तरे मध्ये मध्ये तत्-तद्-अपोहेन । — Other verses of Lord Kṛṣṇa, the Lord of the universe, are interspersed with each other.; गवां श्रुतीनां मार्गे सत्वराः अप्रमत्ता योगिनस् तत्-तद्-उपाध्य्-अपवादेन यथा परं तत्त्वं मृगयन्ते तद्वद् इति भावः ॥१८॥ — This means that the yogis who are quick and careless on the path of the cows and the scriptures seek the Supreme Absolute Truth by excluding the objects of that and that.
18.translation: He argues the type of path-knowledge in terms: ta. Other verses of Lord Kṛṣṇa, the Lord of the universe, are interspersed with each other. This means that the yogis who are quick and careless on the path of the cows and the scriptures seek the Supreme Absolute Truth by excluding the objects of that and that.

19.word_for_word: ततश् च सर्प-शरीर-वेष्टितं कृष्णं दूरान् निरीक्ष्य, गोपांश् च पशूंश् च तथा निरीक्ष्य, आर्ताः परम-कश्मलं परं मोहं प्रापुः ॥१९॥ — Then, looking at Krishna from a distance, wrapped in the body of a snake, and at the cowherd men and cattle in the same way, the distressed men were overcome with great exhaustion and great delusion.
19.translation: Then, looking at Krishna from a distance, wrapped in the body of a snake, and at the cowherd men and cattle in the same way, the distressed men were overcome with great exhaustion and great delusion.

20.word_for_word: प्रियेण श्री-कृष्णेन व्यतिहृतं विरहितं त्रैलोक्यं शून्यं ददृशुः ॥२०.२१॥ — They saw the three worlds empty, deprived of their beloved Lord Krishna.
20.translation: They saw the three worlds empty, deprived of their beloved Lord Krishna.

23.word_for_word: अनन्य-गतिम् आत्मानम् इत्थं निरीक्ष्य, अत एव आत्म-हेतोः स्व-गोकुलम् अतिदुःखितम् आज्ञाय उरङ्ग-बन्धाद् उदतिष्ठद् इत्य् अन्वयः ॥२३॥ — Having thus observed himself as having an exclusive movement, and therefore for his own sake, knowing that his cowherd village was in great distress, he rose up from the bondage of the serpent, as follows.
23.translation: Having thus observed himself as having an exclusive movement, and therefore for his own sake, knowing that his cowherd village was in great distress, he rose up from the bondage of the serpent, as follows.

24.word_for_word: तस्य प्रथ्यमानेन वपुषा व्यथितात्म-शरीरो भुजङ्गः कुण्डलीम् उन्मुच्य तं त्यक्त्वा कुपितः स्व-फणान् उन्नमय्य श्वसन् केवलम् ईक्षमाणस् तस्थौ । — The serpent, whose self-body was distressed by his shattered body, untied his earrings, left him, raised his hoods in anger, and stood breathing heavily, merely staring.; कथं-भूतः ? — How-ever it happened?; श्वसन-रन्ध्रेषु नासा-विवरेषु विषं यस्य स तथा, अम्बरीषो मण्डक-पाक-भाजनं तद्वत् सन्तप्तानि स्तब्धानि ईक्षणानि यस्य स तथा, उल्मुकानि मुखेषु यस्य, स च स च स च ॥२४॥ — He whose poison is in the holes of his breath and in his nostrils is like the vessel for cooking the mandaka, whose eyes are burning and stunned, and whose faces are like meteors, and he is he and he is he.
24.translation: The serpent, whose self-body was distressed by his shattered body, untied his earrings, left him, raised his hoods in anger, and stood breathing heavily, merely staring. How-ever it happened? He whose poison is in the holes of his breath and in his nostrils is like the vessel for cooking the mandaka, whose eyes are burning and stunned, and whose faces are like meteors, and he is he and he is he.

25.word_for_word: हरिश् च क्रीडंस् तम् अमुं सर्वं परिससार परितो बभ्राम । — The monkey played with him and moved around him all around.; अतिकराल-विषाग्नि-युक्ता दृष्टिर् यस्य तम् । — He whose eyes are filled with terrible poisonous fire; जिह्वया द्वि-शिखया इति प्रतिमुखम् ॥२५॥ — The tongue is the opposite of the two-headed.
25.translation: The monkey played with him and moved around him all around. He whose eyes are filled with terrible poisonous fire The tongue is the opposite of the two-headed.

26.word_for_word: एवं परिभ्रमेण एव हतम् ओजो यस्य तम् । — Thus, the energy of the body is killed by the rotation of the body.; उन्नताव् अंसौ यस्य तम् । — whose arms are raised.; तस्य मूर्धसु ये रत्न-निकराः, तेषां स्पर्शेन अत्यरुणं पादाम्बुजं यस्य सः । — He whose feet are very red at the touch of the gems on his heads; ननु, कथं चञ्चलेषु शिरःसु ननर्त ? — Indeed, how did he dance on restless heads?; तत्राह---अखिल-कलानाम् आदि-गुरुः ॥२४॥ — There he says: He is the original master of all arts.
26.translation: Thus, the energy of the body is killed by the rotation of the body. whose arms are raised. He whose feet are very red at the touch of the gems on his heads Indeed, how did he dance on restless heads? There he says: He is the original master of all arts.

27.word_for_word: उपसेदुः प्राप्ताः ॥२७॥ — They approached and arrived.

28.word_for_word: शतैक-शीर्ष्णः शतम् एकानि मुख्यानि शीर्षाणि यस्य, तस्य क्षीणायुषोऽपि पुनर् भ्रमतो यद् यच् छिरो न नमते स्तब्धतां न जहाति । — A hundred-headed man who has one hundred and one main heads, and whose heads do not bow down, does not cease to be stunned, even when his life is exhausted.; नृत्य-च्छलेन अङ्घ्रि-पातैस् तत् तन् ममर्द । — With the trick of dancing, he rubbed it with his kicks.; तदा च आस्यतो मुखेभ्यो नस्तो नासा-विवरेभ्यश् च असृग् वमन् ॥२७॥ — Then he vomited blood from his mouth and nostrils.
28.translation: A hundred-headed man who has one hundred and one main heads, and whose heads do not bow down, does not cease to be stunned, even when his life is exhausted. With the trick of dancing, he rubbed it with his kicks. Then he vomited blood from his mouth and nostrils.

29.word_for_word: पुनर् अपि रुषा उच्चैर् निश्वसतो यद् यत् समुन्नमति, तत् तत् पदाघाते नानुनमयन्न् इह अस्मिन्न् अवसरे हृष्टैर् गन्धर्वादिभिः शेषासनः पुराणः पुरुष इव यशोदा-नन्दनः पुष्पैः प्रपूजितः । — Again, while breathing heavily in anger, they did not bow down to the kick of whatever they could.; यद् वा, तदा गन्धर्वादिभिः पुष्पैः प्रपूजितो गोपैः पुराणः पुमान् इव दृष्ट इति । — Or rather, it is said that the cowherd men, who were then worshiped with flowers by the Gandharvas and others, saw him as an ancient man.; यद् वा, पुष्पैः प्रपूजित इव प्रसन्नः सन् दमयाम्बभूव । — Or rather, he became as pleased as if he had been worshiped with flowers.; हितं कृतवान् इत्य् अर्थः ॥२९॥ — It means that he has done good.
29.translation: Again, while breathing heavily in anger, they did not bow down to the kick of whatever they could. Or rather, it is said that the cowherd men, who were then worshiped with flowers by the Gandharvas and others, saw him as an ancient man. Or rather, he became as pleased as if he had been worshiped with flowers. It means that he has done good.

30.word_for_word: अरणं शरणम् ॥३०॥ — The forest is the refuge.

31.word_for_word: गर्भे जगन्ति यस्य तस्यात्-भारेणावसन्नम् आक्रान्तम् । — The world in its womb is overwhelmed by the weight of the universe.; पार्ष्णिः पाद-पृष्ठम् । — The heel is the back of the foot.; आद्यं श्री-कृष्णम् । — The first is Sri-Krishna.; श्लथन्तो विस्रंसमाना वसनादयो यासां ताः ॥३१॥ — Those whose clothes and other things were slipping and falling apart.
31.translation: The world in its womb is overwhelmed by the weight of the universe. The heel is the back of the foot. The first is Sri-Krishna. Those whose clothes and other things were slipping and falling apart.

32.word_for_word: ताः शरणं प्रपन्नाः सत्यस् तं प्रणेमुः । — They took refuge in him and bowed down to him; सुविग्न-मनसोऽतिविह्वल-चित्ताः । — They are very agitated and very confused.; भुवीति तस्मिन् स्थाने जलाधस्ताद्वा तीरे वा । — Bhuvi is the place under water or on the shore.; शमलस्य पापात्मनोऽपि भर्तुर् मोक्षेप्सवः । — The feast of liberation was the feast of liberation for Shamala, her husband, who was also a sinful soul.; भर्तुर् यच् छमलं तस्य वा । — or whatever is dirty of the husband.; भूत-पतिं प्राणि-मात्रस्य पतिम् । — He is the master of ghosts and the master of all living beings.; शरण-दम् आश्रय-प्रदम् ॥३२॥ — Shelter-giver and shelter-giver.
32.translation: They took refuge in him and bowed down to him They are very agitated and very confused. Bhuvi is the place under water or on the shore. The feast of liberation was the feast of liberation for Shamala, her husband, who was also a sinful soul. or whatever is dirty of the husband. He is the master of ghosts and the master of all living beings. Shelter-giver and shelter-giver.

33.word_for_word:
प्रथमं तावत् कुपितं भगवन्तं दण्डानुमोदनेनोपशमयन्त्यः स्तुवन्ति---न्याय्यो हीति । — First, they appease the Lord, who is so angry, by approving the punishment, and praise Him for being just.; तत्र--- — There; > दण्डानुमोदनं षड्भिर् दशभिश् च हरेर् नतिः । — > Approval of the rod and bowing to the Lord with six and ten.; >
> प्रार्थनं पञ्चभिः श्लोकैस् ततः पन्नग-योषिताम् ॥ — >
> Prayer in five verses and then the woman of the serpent.; न च निग्रहानुग्रह-लक्षणं वैषम्यं तवास्तीत्य् आहुः---धत्से दमम् इति । — Nor do they say that you have any difference in the characteristics of restraint and grace, for you are wearing restraint.; अनुशंसन्न् आलोचयन् ॥३३॥ — recommending and criticizing.
33.translation:
First, they appease the Lord, who is so angry, by approving the punishment, and praise Him for being just. There > Approval of the rod and bowing to the Lord with six and ten. >
> Prayer in five verses and then the woman of the serpent. Nor do they say that you have any difference in the characteristics of restraint and grace, for you are wearing restraint. recommending and criticizing.

34.word_for_word: "निग्रहोऽप्य् अनुग्रहायं" इत्य् उक्तम्, इदानीम् अनुग्रह एवायं न निग्रह इत्य् आहुः, अनुग्रह इति । — It has been said, "Restraint is also for grace," and now they say that grace is not restraint, but grace.; नोऽस्माकम् । — Not ours.; यस्माद् अमुष्य सर्पत्वं दृश्यते, अतस् तन् मूल-पाप-निवर्तको दण्डोऽनुग्रह एव क्रोधत्वेन प्रतीयमानोऽपीत्य् अर्थः ॥३४॥ — Since this man appears to be a serpent, this means that the punishment which destroys that root sin is mercy, even though it is perceived as anger.
34.translation: It has been said, "Restraint is also for grace," and now they say that grace is not restraint, but grace. Not ours. Since this man appears to be a serpent, this means that the punishment which destroys that root sin is mercy, even though it is perceived as anger.

35.word_for_word: महांश् चायम् अनुग्रह इति तस्य पूर्व-पुण्यम् अभिनन्दन्ति, तप इति । — They praise his former merit as great grace and as austerity.; स्वयं मान-रहितेनान्येभ्यो मानदेन च । — Without respect for oneself and with respect for others; सर्वं जीवयतीति सर्व-जीवः ॥३५॥ — The all-living being is the one who gives life to everything.
35.translation: They praise his former merit as great grace and as austerity. Without respect for oneself and with respect for others The all-living being is the one who gives life to everything.

36.word_for_word: न तप-आदि-निमित्त एष भाग्योदयः, किन्त्व् अचिन्त्यं तव कृपा-वैभवम् इत्य् आहुः श्लोक-त्रयेण---कस्यानुभाव इति । — This rise of fortune is not due to austerities and other acts, but to the inconceivable glory of Your grace.; तप-आदिना ब्रह्मादयोऽपि यस्याः श्रियः प्रसादम् इच्छन्ति, सा श्रीर् ललना उत्तमा स्त्री यस्य त्वद्-अङ्घ्रि-स्पर्शाधिकारस्य वाञ्छया तप आचरत् । — The goddess of fortune, whose grace even Brahma and others desire by performing austerities, is the goddess of fortune, the beautiful woman who performed austerities desiring the right to touch Your feet.; अस्य सर्पस्य । — of this snake.; स किं-कृत इति को वेत्तीत्य् अर्थः ॥३६॥ — Who knows what he has done, that is, who knows?
36.translation: This rise of fortune is not due to austerities and other acts, but to the inconceivable glory of Your grace. The goddess of fortune, whose grace even Brahma and others desire by performing austerities, is the goddess of fortune, the beautiful woman who performed austerities desiring the right to touch Your feet. of this snake. Who knows what he has done, that is, who knows?

37.word_for_word: यत् तव पाद-रजः प्रपन्नाः प्राप्ताः पारमेष्ठ्य्-आद्य् अपि तुच्छं मन्यन्ते॥३७॥ — That which even the Supreme Personality of Godhead and others who have surrendered to the dust of Thy feet consider insignificant.
37.translation: That which even the Supreme Personality of Godhead and others who have surrendered to the dust of Thy feet consider insignificant.

38.word_for_word: अहो तद् एषः अयत्नत एव प्राप । — Oh, that’s what he got without effort.; अन्यैः श्च्यादिभिर् अपि । — and by others, such as Schya.; कथं-भूतं पाद-रजः । — How-ever, the foot-dust.; यद् इच्छतः सेव्यं मे भवत्व् इति प्रार्थयमानस्यैव समक्षः प्रत्यक्ष एव विभवोऽपेक्षिता संपद् भवति ॥३८॥ — The power and wealth required is directly present in the presence of the very person who prays, "Let whatever you desire be served to me.
38.translation: Oh, that’s what he got without effort. and by others, such as Schya. How-ever, the foot-dust. The power and wealth required is directly present in the presence of the very person who prays, "Let whatever you desire be served to me.

39.word_for_word: नमस् तुभ्यं भगवते ऽचिन्त्यैश्वर्यादि-गुणाय । — O Lord, You possess inconceivable opulence and other qualities.; तद्-उपपादनाय दशभिः श्लोकैर् विशेषणानि । — To illustrate that, ten verses contain adjectives.; पुरुषाय पूर्ष्व् अन्तर्यामि-रूपेण वर्तमानाय । — To the Supreme Personality of Godhead, who exists in the form of the former and the latter.; महात्मने एवम् अपि नाति-परिच्छिन्नाय । — Even so, the great soul is not too separated.; कुतः ? — Where is it from?; भूतावासाय आकाशाद्य्-आश्रयाय । — For the dwelling of beings, for the shelter of the sky and other things.; एतद् अपि कुतः ।? — Where is this also from.?; भूताय पूर्वम् अपि सते। — Even before the ghost exists.; कुतः ? — Where is it from?; पराय कारणाय । — For the other reason.; किं च, परमात्मने कारणातीताय ॥३९॥ — Moreover, to the Supreme Soul, transcendental to cause.
39.translation: O Lord, You possess inconceivable opulence and other qualities. To illustrate that, ten verses contain adjectives. To the Supreme Personality of Godhead, who exists in the form of the former and the latter. Even so, the great soul is not too separated. Where is it from? For the dwelling of beings, for the shelter of the sky and other things. Where is this also from.? Even before the ghost exists. Where is it from? For the other reason. Moreover, to the Supreme Soul, transcendental to cause.

40.word_for_word: कारणत्वं कारणातीतत्वं च समर्थयितुम् आहुः---ज्ञान-विज्ञान-निधये । — To support causality and transcendence, they say: in the treasury of knowledge and science.; ज्ञानं ज्ञप्तिः, विज्ञानं चिच्-छक्तिः, उभयोर् निधये ताभ्यां पूर्णाय । — Knowledge is knowledge, and science is the power of Chich, in the treasury of both, to be filled with them.; कथं तथात्वम्? — How is that so?; अत उक्तं ब्रह्मणेऽनन्त-शक्तये । — That is why it is said to the infinitely powerful Brahman.; कथं-भूताय ब्रह्मणे ? — How-to the Brahman?; अगुणायाविकाराय । — for the transformation of the unqualified.; कथं-भूताय ? — How-to-be?; अनन्त-शक्तये । — For the infinite power.; प्राकृताय प्रकृति-प्रवर्तकाय, अप्राकृतायेति वा, अप्राकृतानन्त-शक्ति-युक्ताय । — To the natural, the initiator of nature, or to the unnatural, to the unnatural, to the infinitely powerful.; अयम् अर्थः---अगुणत्वाद् अविकारं ब्रह्म-ज्ञप्ति-मात्रत्वात् कारणातीतं प्रकृति-प्रवर्तकोऽनन्त-शक्तिर् विज्ञान-निधित्वाद् ईश्वरः कारणं तद् उभयात्मने नम इति ॥४०॥ — This means that because He is transcendental to causes because He is transcendental because He is transcendental because He is transcendental because He is transcendental because He is transcendental because He is transcendental because He is transcendental because He is transcendental because He is transcendental because He is transcendental to nature and because He is the treasure house of knowledge.
40.translation: To support causality and transcendence, they say: in the treasury of knowledge and science. Knowledge is knowledge, and science is the power of Chich, in the treasury of both, to be filled with them. How is that so? That is why it is said to the infinitely powerful Brahman. How-to the Brahman? for the transformation of the unqualified. How-to-be? For the infinite power. To the natural, the initiator of nature, or to the unnatural, to the unnatural, to the infinitely powerful. This means that because He is transcendental to causes because He is transcendental because He is transcendental because He is transcendental because He is transcendental because He is transcendental because He is transcendental because He is transcendental because He is transcendental because He is transcendental because He is transcendental to nature and because He is the treasure house of knowledge.

41.word_for_word: अनन्त-शक्तित्वात् काल-शक्त्या विश्व-स्रष्टृत्वादि-रूपेण नमस्यन्ति । — Because of His infinite power, they worship Him in the form of the power of time, the creator of the universe, and so on.; कालाय काल-स्वरूपाय । — For time, for the form of time.; काल-नाभाय काल-शक्त्याश्रयाय । — O navel of time, O shelter of the power of time.; कालावयवानां सृष्ट्य्-आदि-समयानां साक्षिणे । — You are the witness of the times of creation and the beginning of the elements of time.; ततश् च विश्वाय विश्व-रूपाय । — and then to the universe, the universal form.; तर्हि किं जडोऽहम् । — So why am I dumb?; नहि, तद् उपद्रष्टे । — No, that’s the observer.; न च द्रष्टृ-मात्राय, किन्तु तत् कर्त्रे । — And not only to the seer, but to the doer.; न च कर्तृ-मात्राय, विश्व-हेतवे सर्व-कारक-रूपाय ॥४१॥ — nor to the doer alone, but to the cause of the universe and to the form of all causes.
41.translation: Because of His infinite power, they worship Him in the form of the power of time, the creator of the universe, and so on. For time, for the form of time. O navel of time, O shelter of the power of time. You are the witness of the times of creation and the beginning of the elements of time. and then to the universe, the universal form. So why am I dumb? No, that’s the observer. And not only to the seer, but to the doer. nor to the doer alone, but to the cause of the universe and to the form of all causes.

42.word_for_word: तद् एवाहुः, भूत-मात्रेन्द्रिय-प्राण-मनो-बुद्ध्य्-आशयात्मने, आशयश् चित्तम्, भूतादि-रूपाय, अतः सर्व-कारक-रूपायेति । — That is what they say, the beings, the senses, the life-force, the mind, the intellect, the intention, the self, the intention, the mind, in the form of beings and other things, and therefore in the form of all causes.; अहङ्कारात्मतया नमस्यन्ति, त्रि-गुणेनेति । — They will bow down to the ego-self, and to the threefold.; एवं सृष्टे कार्ये यस् त्रि-गुणोऽभिमानस् तेन गूढा स्वंश-भूतानाम् आत्मनां जीवानाम् अनुभूतिर् येन तस्मै ॥४२॥ — The threefold egoism in the work thus created by Him conceals the perception of the living entities as parts of Himself.
42.translation: That is what they say, the beings, the senses, the life-force, the mind, the intellect, the intention, the self, the intention, the mind, in the form of beings and other things, and therefore in the form of all causes. They will bow down to the ego-self, and to the threefold. The threefold egoism in the work thus created by Him conceals the perception of the living entities as parts of Himself.

43.word_for_word: त्वं त्व् अहङ्कारानावृत इति स्तुवन्ति । — They praise You, saying, “You are covered by egoism.”; नमोऽनन्ताय, अहङ्कारापरिच्छेदात् । — Obeisance to the Infinite, who is separated from the ego.; अतः सूक्ष्माय, अदृश्यत्वात् । — Therefore, to the subtle, because it is invisible.; अत एव कूट-स्थाय, उपाधि-कृत-विकाराभावात् । — That is why it is in the code, since there is no transformation caused by the title.; अत एव विपश्चिते सर्व-ज्ञाय । — That is why the wise know everything.; एवं वस्तुतः स्तुत्वाचिन्त्य-मायात्वेन स्तुवन्ति, नाना-वादानुरोधाय । — Thus, in fact, they praise Him as an inconceivable illusion, in order to refute various arguments.; अस्ति नास्ति सर्व-ज्ञः किञ्चिज्-ज्ञो बद्धो मुक्त एकोऽनेक इत्य्-आदि-नाना-वादान् अनुरुणद्धि माययानुवर्तते यस् तस्मै । — There is nothing, there is nothing, there is nothing, there is nothing, there is nothing, there is nothing, there is nothing, there is nothing, there is nothing, there is nothing, there is nothing, there is one, there is nothing.; किं च, वाच्य-वाचक-शक्तये । — What is more, for the power of speech and expression.; अभिधानाभिधेय-शक्ति-भेदाद् अपि नानात्वेन प्रतीयमानायेत्य् अर्थः ॥४३॥ — This means that it is perceived as diverse even from the difference in the power of the object to be addressed.
43.translation: They praise You, saying, “You are covered by egoism.” Obeisance to the Infinite, who is separated from the ego. Therefore, to the subtle, because it is invisible. That is why it is in the code, since there is no transformation caused by the title. That is why the wise know everything. Thus, in fact, they praise Him as an inconceivable illusion, in order to refute various arguments. There is nothing, there is nothing, there is nothing, there is nothing, there is nothing, there is nothing, there is nothing, there is nothing, there is nothing, there is nothing, there is nothing, there is one, there is nothing. What is more, for the power of speech and expression. This means that it is perceived as diverse even from the difference in the power of the object to be addressed.

44.word_for_word: अनावृतत्वम् एव हेत्व्-अन्तरेणापि सूचयन्त्यः स्तुवन्ति, नमः प्रमाण-मूलाय चक्षुर्-आदीनां चक्षुर्-आदि-रूपाय । — They praise the uncoveredness itself, even by the difference of cause, saying, Obeisance to the root of proof, the form of the eyes and the eyes of the eyes and the others.; अत एव कवये स्वयं तन् निरपेक्ष-ज्ञानाय । — That is why the poet himself has to know it absolutely.; कुतः ? — Where is it from?; शास्त्र-योनये वेदात्मक-निःश्वासाय । — For the Vedic breath in the womb of the scriptures.; किं च, प्रवृत्ताय निवृत्ताय निगमाय नमो नमः ॥४४॥ — What is more, I offer my obeisances to the Vedas, to the initiated and the withdrawn.
44.translation: They praise the uncoveredness itself, even by the difference of cause, saying, Obeisance to the root of proof, the form of the eyes and the eyes of the eyes and the others. That is why the poet himself has to know it absolutely. Where is it from? For the Vedic breath in the womb of the scriptures. What is more, I offer my obeisances to the Vedas, to the initiated and the withdrawn.

45.word_for_word: किं च, अनावृतैश्वर्यत्वाद् एव चतुर्-मूर्ति-रूपेण सर्वोपास्यत्वेन नमन्ति, नमः कृष्णायेति श्लोकेन । — Moreover, because of His uncovered opulence, they bow down to Him in the form of the four idols, who are worshiped by all, with the verse 'Om Kṛṣṇayaye'; रामाय सङ्कर्षणाय । — O Rāma, O Sankarṣaṇa.; वसुदेव-सुताय च । — and to the son of Vasudeva.; वसुदेव-शब्दितं शुद्धं सत्त्वं तत्र प्रकाशमानाय वासुदेवायेत्य् अर्थः । — The word Vasudeva means the pure Sattva, who is illuminated there by Vāsudeva.; सात्वताम् उपासकानां पतये सालोक्यादिना-पालकाय । — O lord of the devotees of the Sātvatas, O protector of the worlds and other things,; एवं चतुर्-मूर्तये कृष्णाय तुभ्यं नम इति ॥४५॥ — Thus I offer my obeisances unto You, O four-forming Lord Kṛṣṇa.
45.translation: Moreover, because of His uncovered opulence, they bow down to Him in the form of the four idols, who are worshiped by all, with the verse 'Om Kṛṣṇayaye' O Rāma, O Sankarṣaṇa. and to the son of Vasudeva. The word Vasudeva means the pure Sattva, who is illuminated there by Vāsudeva. O lord of the devotees of the Sātvatas, O protector of the worlds and other things, Thus I offer my obeisances unto You, O four-forming Lord Kṛṣṇa.

46.word_for_word: कथं चतुर्-मुर्तितेति तद् आहुः, नमो गुण-प्रदीपायेति । — How is it that they call it the four-image, and that it is the lamp of the modes of nature?; गुणा अन्तः-करणानि तानि प्रदीपयति प्रकाशयतीति तथा तस्मै । — The modes of nature illuminate and illuminate the inner actions of the Supreme Personality of Godhead.; चित्ताद्य्-अधिष्ठातृत्वेन चतुर्-मूर्तितेत्य् अर्थः । — This means that the four-image is the possessor of the mind and other things.; ननु, तथाप्य् एकस्यैव कथं चतुष्ट्वम् अत आहुः, गुणात्म-च्छादनाय तैर् एव गुणैर् उपासकानां फल-वैचित्र्यायात्मानम् आच्छाद्य नानात्वेन प्रकाशम् आनायेत्य् अर्थः । — Indeed, how can there be fourness of the same one? Therefore, they say, that in order to cover the Self of the modes of nature, the same modes of nature cover the Self of the fruits and peculiarities of the worshipers and bring light to them in their diversity.; ननु, तर्हि कथं प्रतीतिर् अत उक्तम्, गुण-वृत्त्य्-उपलक्ष्याय चित्तादीनां चेतनाध्यवसायादि-वृत्तिभिर् उपलक्ष्याय । — If so, then how is perception, as stated above, to be perceived by the instincts of the mind and others, such as the determination of consciousness?; उपलक्षणम् एवाहुः, गुण-द्रष्ट्रे तत् साक्षिणे । — They say that it is a sub-characteristic, in the seer of the qualities and in the witness.; कथञ्चिद् उपलक्ष्य एव न ज्ञेय इत्य् आहुः, स्व-संविदे, अगोचरायेत्य् अर्थः ॥४६॥ — They say that it is not to be known only by perceiving it in some way, in its own consciousness, meaning that it is invisible.
46.translation: How is it that they call it the four-image, and that it is the lamp of the modes of nature? The modes of nature illuminate and illuminate the inner actions of the Supreme Personality of Godhead. This means that the four-image is the possessor of the mind and other things. Indeed, how can there be fourness of the same one? Therefore, they say, that in order to cover the Self of the modes of nature, the same modes of nature cover the Self of the fruits and peculiarities of the worshipers and bring light to them in their diversity. If so, then how is perception, as stated above, to be perceived by the instincts of the mind and others, such as the determination of consciousness? They say that it is a sub-characteristic, in the seer of the qualities and in the witness. They say that it is not to be known only by perceiving it in some way, in its own consciousness, meaning that it is invisible.

47.word_for_word: अगोचरत्वम् उपलक्ष्यत्वं च दर्शयन्त्यो नमन्ति, अव्याकृत-विहाराय, अतर्क्य-महिम्न इत्य् अर्थः । — They bow down, showing invisibility and subtlety, to the unmanifest pastime, to the irrational glory.; सर्व-व्याकृत-सिद्धये सर्व-कार्योत्पत्ति-प्रकाश-हेतुत्वेनोपलक्षण-योग्यायेत्य् अर्थः । — This means that it is worthy of being characterized as the cause of the light of the origin of all actions for the accomplishment of all manifestations.; उपलक्षणान्तरम् आहुः---हे हृषीकेश ! — They say of the other sub-characteristic: O Hrishikesh!; करण-प्रवर्तक ! — Karan-pravartaka!; किं विषयैप्सया ? — What about the desire for objects?; न, मुनये आत्मा-रामाय । — No, to the sage Atma-Rama.; किं साधन-वशेन वा ? — Is it means-dependent?; न हि, मौन-शीलिने मौनम् आत्मा-रामता तत्-स्वभावाय ॥४७॥ — Indeed, silence for the silent is not self-pleasure for that nature.
47.translation: They bow down, showing invisibility and subtlety, to the unmanifest pastime, to the irrational glory. This means that it is worthy of being characterized as the cause of the light of the origin of all actions for the accomplishment of all manifestations. They say of the other sub-characteristic: O Hrishikesh! Karan-pravartaka! What about the desire for objects? No, to the sage Atma-Rama. Is it means-dependent? Indeed, silence for the silent is not self-pleasure for that nature.

48.word_for_word: कुतः ? — Where is it from?; परावर-गति-ज्ञाय स्थूल-सूक्ष्माणां गति-ज्ञत्वेन, क्वापि सज् जमानायेत्य् अर्थः । — By knowing the movements of the higher and the lower, and by knowing the movements of the gross and the subtle, it means to be ready somewhere.; अपि च सर्वाध्यक्षाय सर्वस्याधिष्ठात्रे । — Moreover, He is the presiding deity of all and the possessor of all.; कुत एतत् ? — Where is this?; अविश्वाय न विश्वं यस्मिंस् तन् निषेधावधये । — Forbidden to kill the unbeliever in whom the universe is not.; विश्वाय च तद्-विवर्ताधिष्ठानायेत्य् अर्थः । — This means that the universe is the source of its transformation.; किं च, तद्-दृअष्ट्रे अध्यासापवाद-साक्षिणे । — What’s more, it’s a witness to the exceptions to the study.; अपि च, अस्य विश्वाध्यासस्य तद्-अपवादस्य चाविद्याविद्याभ्यां हेतवे। — Moreover, for the sake of this universal doctrine and its exception by both ignorance and ignorance.; यद् वा, अविश्वाय विश्व-तैजसाद्य्-अवस्था-रहिताय । — That is, for the unbeliever, who is devoid of the state of cosmic effulgence.; विश्वाय च माय्या स्वंशैस् तत्-तद्-अवस्थाय तद्-द्रष्ट्रे तासाम् अवस्थानां भावाभाव-साक्षिणे । — The illusory energy manifests itself in its own parts to the universe, to the seer of its various states, and to the witness of the existence and absence of those states.; अन्यत् समानम् । — Otherwise the same.; तस्मात् सर्व-गति-ज्ञत्व-सर्वाधिष्ठातृत्वात्मा-रामत्वादिभिर् निरतिशयैश्वर्याय तुभ्यं नम इति । — Therefore, I offer my obeisances to You, who are infinitely omnipotent in Your knowledge of all movements, Your possession of all things, Your self-realization and Your attainment of all pleasure.; विशेषणैर् असङ्कीर्णैः पञ्च-पञ्चा-शतान् अतः । — Therefore, five hundred and fifty are not narrowed down by adjectives.; अहि-स्त्रीभिः प्रसन्नो वस् तासाम् इव भवेद् धरिः ॥४८॥ — The earth will be pleased with the women of the snakes as if they were their clothes.
48.translation: Where is it from? By knowing the movements of the higher and the lower, and by knowing the movements of the gross and the subtle, it means to be ready somewhere. Moreover, He is the presiding deity of all and the possessor of all. Where is this? Forbidden to kill the unbeliever in whom the universe is not. This means that the universe is the source of its transformation. What’s more, it’s a witness to the exceptions to the study. Moreover, for the sake of this universal doctrine and its exception by both ignorance and ignorance. That is, for the unbeliever, who is devoid of the state of cosmic effulgence. The illusory energy manifests itself in its own parts to the universe, to the seer of its various states, and to the witness of the existence and absence of those states. Otherwise the same. Therefore, I offer my obeisances to You, who are infinitely omnipotent in Your knowledge of all movements, Your possession of all things, Your self-realization and Your attainment of all pleasure. Therefore, five hundred and fifty are not narrowed down by adjectives. The earth will be pleased with the women of the snakes as if they were their clothes.

49.word_for_word: एवं तवद् दण्डानुमोदनेन नमस्कारैश् च भगवन्तं प्रसाद्येदानीं त्वद् अधीनानां प्राणिनां कोऽपराध इत्य् आशयवत्यः प्रार्थयन्ते, त्वं हीति । — Thus, by approving of your punishment and by offering obeisances to the Supreme Personality of Godhead, those who are under Your control are now praying to You, intending to know what is the fault of Your subjects.; अस्य लोकस्य जन्मादि त्वम् एव अकृतऽकरोः, ततश् च तांस् तान् संस्कार-रूपेण सतः स्वभावान् घोरत्वादीन् प्रतिबोधयन्न् ईहसे क्रीडसि । — You yourself did not cause the birth of this world, and then you play with them in the form of rituals, reminding them of the horrible nature of the truth.; यद् वा, अस्य जन्मादींस् त्वम् ईहस इत्य् अन्वयः । — Or rather, it follows that you are the beginning of his birth.; कथं-भूतः । — How-ever.; अकृतानादिर्या काल-शक्तिस् तां धारयतीति तथा । — And so it is that the power of time, which is the beginning of the uncreated, holds it.; अन्यत् समानम् ॥४९॥ — Otherwise the same.
49.translation: Thus, by approving of your punishment and by offering obeisances to the Supreme Personality of Godhead, those who are under Your control are now praying to You, intending to know what is the fault of Your subjects. You yourself did not cause the birth of this world, and then you play with them in the form of rituals, reminding them of the horrible nature of the truth. Or rather, it follows that you are the beginning of his birth. How-ever. And so it is that the power of time, which is the beginning of the uncreated, holds it. Otherwise the same.

50.word_for_word: अतस् तस्य तवैवामूस् तनवस् तन्यन्त इति क्रीडोपस्कराः । — Therefore, his sporting equipment is stretched out like yours.; तथापि तवाधुना शान्ताः प्रियाः । — However, your dear ones are now calm.; कुतः ? — Where is it from?; सतां धर्म-परिपालनेच्छया ईहतः प्रवर्तमानस्य, अतस् तान् अवितुं स्थातुः स्थितस्य ॥५०॥ — He who is endeavoring to observe the righteousness of the virtuous and who therefore stands firm to protect them.
50.translation: Therefore, his sporting equipment is stretched out like yours. However, your dear ones are now calm. Where is it from? He who is endeavoring to observe the righteousness of the virtuous and who therefore stands firm to protect them.

51.word_for_word: एवं तवाप्रियाचरणाद्य्-अपराधस् तर्हि सोढव्य इति ॥५१.५२॥ — Thus the offense of acting unpleasantly to you should then be tolerated.
51.translation: Thus the offense of acting unpleasantly to you should then be tolerated.

53.word_for_word: युष्मद्-अनुग्रहेऽन्येषां मृत्युर् एवेति चेत् तन् नेत्य् आहुः, विधेहीति । — If it is at your mercy that others die, they say that it is not, and that it is forbidden.; त्वद्-आज्ञया प्राणिनो नाद्याम् एति भावः ॥५३-५५॥ — This means that by Thy command the living being does not come to the beginning.53-5
53.translation: If it is at your mercy that others die, they say that it is not, and that it is forbidden. This means that by Thy command the living being does not come to the beginning.53-5

56.word_for_word: यद् असद्-ग्रह इति । — That is, the planet of evil.; यतः स्वभावोऽसद्-ग्रह-रूपः । — Because nature is in the form of an evil planet.; यद् वा, यतः स्वभावाद् असति देहादौ ग्रहः स दुस्त्यज इति ॥५६॥ — That is, because by its nature the planet in the beginning of the body is not present, it is difficult to give up.
56.translation: That is, the planet of evil. Because nature is in the form of an evil planet. That is, because by its nature the planet in the beginning of the body is not present, it is difficult to give up.

57.word_for_word: गुणैर् विविधतया सृज्यत इति गुण-विसर्जनम् । — The dissolution of the modes of nature is the process of creating the modes of nature in various ways.; तत्रापि नाना-स्वभावादयो यस्य तत् ॥५७॥ — Even there, that which has various nature and others.
57.translation: The dissolution of the modes of nature is the process of creating the modes of nature in various ways. Even there, that which has various nature and others.

58.word_for_word: जात्या जन्मनैवोरुर् मन्युर् येषां ते वयं स्वयं कथं त्यजामः ॥५८ — How can we ourselves abandon those whose thighs are not angered by birth or race?
58.translation: How can we ourselves abandon those whose thighs are not angered by birth or race?

59.word_for_word: हि यस्मात् तत्र त्वन्-माया-त्यागे भवान् एव कारणम् इत्य् अनुग्रहं विधेहि ममाज्ञया खादन्तीति । — For since you are the cause of the renunciation of your illusory energy there, please grant them mercy, for they are eating at my command.; ईश्वरत्वान् निग्रहं वा विधेहीति ॥५९॥ — Being a lord or restraining him, he said.
59.translation: For since you are the cause of the renunciation of your illusory energy there, please grant them mercy, for they are eating at my command. Being a lord or restraining him, he said.

60.word_for_word: यतो गोभिर् नृभिश् च नदी भुज्यत इति ॥६०॥ — Because the river is fed by cows and men, it is said.
60.translation: Because the river is fed by cows and men, it is said.

61.word_for_word: न युष्मत्तो भयम् आप्नुयात् । — He should not be afraid of you.; तस्य युष्माभिर् भयं नोत्पादनीयम् इत्य् आज्ञा ॥६१.६२॥ — You should not instill fear in him, is the command.
61.translation: He should not be afraid of you. You should not instill fear in him, is the command.

62.word_for_word: इतोऽपि त्वया निर्गन्तव्यम् इत्य् आह---योऽस्मिन्न् इति । — You must also get out of here,” he said, “who is in this.”; त्वयि स्थिते तन् न सम्भवतीति भावः ॥६२॥ — This means that when You are present that is not possible.
62.translation: You must also get out of here,” he said, “who is in this.” This means that when You are present that is not possible.

63.word_for_word: न च तव गरुड-भयं भवेद् इत्य् आह---द्वीपम् इति ॥६३॥ — And you will not be afraid of Garuda, he said, and said, "It is an island.
63.translation: And you will not be afraid of Garuda, he said, and said, "It is an island.
